extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents before the USPTO), OED staff, and parties involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and sanctions governing discipline of practitioners registered to practice patent matters before the USPTO, including specific regulatory violations, procedural steps for probation/suspension, publication and notification requirements, and mitigating/aggravating factors considered in sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.40(b)(2) — Decline employment when incompetent
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must decline employment when the employment would result in failure to competently prosecute the patent applications of current clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged violation by not declining employment from new clients when doing so would have resulted in failing to competently prosecute existing clients' applications (managing ~1,000 applications on his docket). This rule supports workload-management as part of competent representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — Do not allow client applications to be abandoned without instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not allow client patent applications to go abandoned without the respective client's knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent admitted seven patent applications became abandoned without client knowledge or consent; permitting abandonment without client instruction violates this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to maintain competent docketing and workload systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are expected to maintain reliable docketing and case-management practices to avoid missed deadlines and unintended abandonments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As remedial and illustrative measures, the respondent implemented: an electronic docketing system to track extendible and non-extendible deadlines; a paper docketing system as a secondary back-up; verifying deadlines by checking the USPTO Private PAIR online system; and off-site electronic backups. These are presented as best-practice examples to satisfy the competence obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available for disciplinary violations
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may impose public reprimands, probation, and suspension (among other sanctions) for violations of the disciplinary rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the agreed sanction was a public reprimand and twelve (12) months' probation. The Office also reserves the ability to seek suspension for up to twelve (12) months if probation conditions or disciplinary rules are violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and 15-day response procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply with the Final Order or disciplinary rules during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause and grant the practitioner fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause is sent to the practitioner's last address of record pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a). The OED Director considers the practitioner's response (if any) before deciding whether to proceed to request suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's referral/request for suspension to USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 15-day response period and consideration of any response, if the OED Director remains of the opinion that the practitioner failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, the practitioner's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request entry of an immediate suspension for up to twelve (12) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the procedural step from OED to the USPTO Director to effect suspension based on probation violations or other misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspension regarding USPTO customer numbers and PKI
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended, the practitioner shall be dissociated from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates and may not use or obtain USPTO customer numbers or PKI certificates unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon suspension the USPTO will promptly dissociate the practitioner's name from customer numbers and PKI certificates; the practitioner may not use or obtain them until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders and disciplinary notices shall be published by the OED Director in the OED Reading Room and in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This matter required the OED Director to publish the Final Order electronically at the OED Reading Room and to publish a Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation in the Official Gazette, including factual recitals and the rule violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to affected foreign representatives and affidavit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4), the practitioner must, within 30 days of the Final Order, provide a copy of the Final Order to the foreign representatives of current clients whose applications became abandoned, and within 45 days provide an affidavit to the OED Director stating that such clients were notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a post-discipline compliance obligation imposed on the practitioner to notify affected foreign representatives and verify notification to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's right to seek further discipline and use of record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the agreement prevents the Office from seeking further discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57 for misconduct on which an Order to Show Cause is issued, or from considering the record of the proceeding (including the Final Order) in future disciplinary matters as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may rely on this disciplinary record in addressing subsequent complaints or in future proceedings to increase sanctions or counter representations by the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating and aggravating factors considered in sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors such as absence of prior disciplinary history, cooperation with the Office, sincere contrition, remedial measures taken, and evidence of generally providing quality legal services may mitigate sanctions; repeated or similar misconduct may aggravate future sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes respondent's lack of prior disciplinary history, cooperation, contrition, remedial docketing changes, continued client relationships, and absence of subsequent complaints as mitigating considerations that influenced the agreed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement terms including allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlements between the practitioner and the Office may specify terms regarding sanctions, compliance obligations, and allocation of costs; in this agreement each party bears its own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly states that the OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement; settlement terms may therefore include discrete compliance and cost provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director's jurisdiction over practitioner discipline is grounded in statutes and regulations such as 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutory and regulatory provisions as the basis for the Office's authority to approve settlement agreements and impose disciplinary sanctions.
